extracted.intended_audience: general readers and those researching television production, live-broadcast stunts, and broadcast safety
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted safety- and production-related standards and lessons from a Wikipedia article about a live British variety show whose on-air stunts led to injuries and a fatality. Focus is on criteria relevant to planning, rehearsing, and running live TV stunts safely and lawfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of safety officers during stunts/rehearsals
rubrics_metrics.description: The coroner recommended that safety officers be on hand during any such future stunts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safety officers should be physically present at rehearsals and live performances rather than merely consulted by telephone; absence of the safety officer was cited as a failure in the Michael Lush case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional stunt supervision / trained stuntman involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: There was no supervision or demonstration from a trained stuntman, and the escapologist retained as trainer was only experienced with theatrical tricks and had not performed the stunt required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have appropriately experienced stunt coordinators/trainers run rehearsals and supervise the stunt; theatrical or non-specialist experience is insufficient for complex/ hazardous stunts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate safety equipment (airbag / safety net)
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional rehearsals should have used an airbag in case of falls; there was no airbag or safety net to cushion a hazardous fall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure crash-attenuation devices (airbags, nets) are in place for high-risk stunts; omission of such equipment is a critical safety failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redundant rigging and secure connectors (multiple ropes / shackles)
rubrics_metrics.description: A similar stunt had used three ropes as opposed to the one rope used by the BBC, and used shackles in place of carabiner clips; the carabiner clip sprang loose during the fatal jump.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design rigging with redundancy (multiple independent lines), use hardware rated for the application (prefer shackles or other proven connectors), and avoid single-point-failure attachment methods like a lone carabiner where professionals use multiple attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough equipment testing and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Graham Games of the HSE demonstrated that the clip could have been opened by the weight of a bag of sugar and that the clip sprang loose fourteen times in twenty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test all rigging and connectors under load conditions, document failures and retest after fixes; do not rely on untested or suspect equipment for live stunts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient rehearsal time and professional timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Stunt experts said even professional rehearsals should have taken weeks rather than days; producer rehearsed in too short a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate adequate rehearsal time proportional to stunt complexity; compressing rehearsal schedules increases risk and is an anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear communication and contingency/abort procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: There was no way for Lush to contact the ground once he was in the air, and nobody in the air with him in case he changed his mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish and test in-air communication, abort signals, and contingency personnel (e.g., partners in position) so participants can stop an unsafe stunt; absence of these measures contributed to the tragedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid exposing untrained members of the public to high-risk stunts
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC managing director stated there would be no future programmes that exposed members of the public to risk; the show had used volunteers for dangerous stunts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer professional performers for hazardous stunts; using volunteers from the public for life‑threatening acts is discouraged and may lead to legal and ethical issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit or control participant impairment and unsuitable attire/footwear
rubrics_metrics.description: Lush had drunk two pints of beer at lunch prior to the rehearsal; he was wearing wet boots before he jumped, which was a safety hazard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce rules prohibiting alcohol/drug use before stunts; ensure participants wear appropriate, dry footwear and clothing appropriate to the stunt; monitor participant readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid use of inadvisable materials (e.g., elasticated bungee ropes) against expert advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Despite advice against it, the BBC production team insisted on the use of an elasticated bungee rope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow expert recommendations on materials and equipment; do not override safety advice from qualified specialists for production expediency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and regulatory compliance (Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 / HSE standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC was prosecuted by the HSE for breaches of the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974; the HSE had previously threatened legal action to stop planned stunts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure compliance with applicable workplace and public-safety regulations and HSE guidance; failure to comply can lead to prosecution, fines, and reputational damage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management responsibility and safety culture
rubrics_metrics.description: The jury was informed of several failures on the part of the BBC: safety officer not present, inadequate supervision, ignoring advice. BBC leadership later stated they would not continue programmes exposing the public to risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producers and senior management must prioritize safety, heed expert advice, ensure qualified personnel and equipment are provided, and create a culture where safety cannot be overridden by programming pressures.
